claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr has a crystalline BCC state.
A specimen containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen represents a realistic trace-oxygen condition for HfNbTaTiZr.
Prior HfNbTaTiZr calculations modeled defect-free bulk crystals.
A coupled DFT and MD framework can explicitly incorporate atomic-mass, force-constant, and local-vibrational-mode variations.
Explicit electron–phonon coupling will allow separate computation of lattice and electronic thermal conductivities.
Below 200 K, lattice and electronic heat-transport contributions in HfNbTaTiZr are comparable.
The 300–1200 K regime matches available thermal-conductivity measurements for HfNbTaTiZr.
Component variability and minor oxygen impurities produce a distorted lattice with altered local vibrational dynamics and electron–phonon interactions.
Replacing a single-parameter Debye approximation with explicit quantum-mechanical treatment of phonons and electrons captures anharmonic scattering.
Capturing anharmonic scattering and local vibrational-mode variations will improve separation and accuracy of lattice and electronic conductivity predictions.
The proposed framework will reduce predictive error by approximately 20–30% relative to traditional analytical models.
Predicted lattice and electronic conductivities will converge with experiment in both the below-200 K and 300–1200 K regimes.
Traditional models use perfect defect-free crystals, a single Debye temperature, or averaged DFT-derived elastic properties.
Traditional models conflate lattice and electronic contributions and have larger predictive uncertainties.
The method is applicable only to polycrystalline or near-single-crystalline HfNbTaTiZr with trace oxygen.
The method's accuracy for amorphous, highly disordered, or heavily contaminated samples is unverified.
Uncertainty in electron–phonon coupling parameters and impurity effects may change the predicted improvement.
Inelastic neutron scattering or Raman spectroscopy can provide phonon information for evaluating the lattice contribution.
Electrical resistivity can be used to infer the electronic thermal-conductivity contribution.
Failure to achieve at least a 20–30% error reduction relative to traditional models would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The proposed initial state is described both as defect-free bulk and as containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen. A crystal containing interstitial or substitutional oxygen is not strictly defect-free.
